raw_response:
*(Reasoning in my own voice — I'm the old man who farms these 5 mu.)*

Sixty years I've been on this land. Me and the old lady, we're the only ones left here now — the kids went to the city a long time ago, they send money sometimes. So it's just us two and our 5 mu. My back don't work like it used to, so I can't do the heavy work no more. What I do, like most of us old folks around here, is hire the tractor man when it's time to plow and plant, and the big combine when it's time to harvest. Costs some money but there's no way around it.

**Wheat.** Goes in the ground early October, same as always. I buy a sack of seed at the shop — whatever Jimai variety they've got that year, the neighbors all use it. Before the tractor man comes to sow, I spread compound fertilizer, about 2 bags per mu — that's the 15-15-15 kind, blue bags. Then in spring, when the wheat wakes up from the cold, I put on urea before the first watering, about one sack across 3 mu. My second son told me once on the phone that the extension guy in the city says you can use less, but I've always done it this way and the wheat comes up fine. I'm not changing now.

**Watering the wheat.** The well is right there in the corner of the field, but pumping costs electricity, and electric ain't cheap. I water three times — once after green-up, once at jointing, once when the grain's filling. Some of the younger fellas skip the last one if it's been rainy, but I don't take chances. I lived through the dry years. One missed watering and the grain comes out shriveled.

**Maize.** As soon as the combine takes off the wheat in June, the tractor man comes straight back and drills maize into the stubble. Can't wait even a week — the summer's short and if you plant late the frost catches you. Hybrid maize seed from the shop, about 50 yuan a bag. The ground still has fertilizer left from the wheat so I don't put much at planting. When the maize gets to my knee, I spread urea between the rows, maybe 20 kg per mu.

**Watering the maize.** Depends on the sky. A wet summer, I don't water at all. Most years I water once, maybe twice if August goes dry.

**Spray.** Herbicide once on each crop — saves me bending over pulling weeds, my knees can't take it. On the maize I also spray once for the borer around tasseling time because my neighbor's field got hit bad two years ago and I didn't want the same thing happening to mine.

**What I expect.** Wheat about 400 kg per mu in a normal year. Maize 450 or so. Together from 5 mu it's enough grain to eat, feed the chickens, and sell what's left. It's not much money but we don't need much. As long as nothing goes wrong, we manage.
